glance_takeaway: This page is about a research project called 'murmur' that tests whether cheap, natural-reverb-style audio augmentations can beat using a bigger model for bird-call classification on a small, long-tailed dataset (34 species). At a glance it says the bet 'partially works': across 6 experiments the best validation macro-F1 improved from 0.612 to 0.671 (+5.9), but the gain is modest and concentrated in common species while the rare tail barely moves, so the next step is to augment per class. There is a horizontal flow diagram summarizing the story and a line/bar chart of validation macro-F1 across experiments.

F1.note: Title 'cheap augmentation vs a bigger model' + framing text state both the augmentation-helps and beats-a-bigger-model bet; final caption names 'H2 (aug beats a bigger model per unit compute)'.

F2.note: Only '34 species' appears (flow node). No 6,200 clips, 5-sec/32 kHz, or 128-mel log-mel spec on the page.

F3.note: No 70/15/15 split or ~930 val/test counts; only a passing 'test split stays untouched' in the final caption.

F4.note: Qualitative 'Small data, long-tailed' label and the steep per-species F1 gradient are shown, but none of the imbalance numbers (Robin 480, 11<80, 5<45, median 120, 8=52%).

F5.note: 'Validation macro-F1' is the section heading and chart title; caption states 'Seed-to-seed noise is about +/-0.006'.

F6.note: Ledger node 'exp-01 baseline no aug · 0.612'; trajectory baseline bar at 0.612.

F7.note: Ledger node 'exp-02 light reverb · 0.641 win'; RT60/p params omitted but value and 'first win' conveyed.

F8.note: Ledger node 'exp-03 pitch + stretch · 0.589 regression', below-baseline dip visible in trajectory chart.

F9.note: Ledger node 'exp-04 noise mixing · 0.643 null'; caption 'null alone but composed usefully'. Exact +0.002 not stated.

F10.note: Ledger node 'exp-05 full stack · 0.671 BEST'; caption lists stack = reverb + noise + SpecAugment + partial balanced sampler.

F11.note: Ledger node 'exp-06 heavy reverb · 0.663 common-only', below best; 'common-only' label conveys head-only benefit.

F12.note: Ledger caption: 'exp-03 (pitch/time warp) regressed below baseline by smearing rare-class cues'. The <50-clips detail is omitted but the mechanism is conveyed.

F13.note: Caption: exp-04 'was null alone but composed usefully inside exp-05's stack'. Exact +0.002 vs +-0.006 comparison not shown but null + kept-because-composes conveyed.

F14.note: Stack components (light reverb + noise mix + SpecAugment + partial balanced sampler) conveyed via exp-05 node/caption; pitch/stretch and heavy reverb shown as off (dropped / below best). Exact hyperparameters and 'Small CNN unchanged control' omitted.

F15.note: Per-species chart bars [0.85,0.83,0.74,0.54,0.33] vs baseline line [0.79,0.76,0.68,0.51,0.34] match source exactly; caption notes Wood Thrush +0.03 and Kirtland 0.34->0.33 regression.

render_issues: Minor: on both xychart-beta charts the rotated y-axis title ('macro-F1' / 'F1') overlaps the y-axis tick numbers (mermaid quirk), and the metric-trajectory chart plots an identical bar and line series (redundant encoding). Nothing is broken or illegible.
strengths: Highly faithful ledger: every experiment value (0.612/0.641/0.589/0.643/0.671/0.663) and the per-species numbers match the source exactly, with honest labels (win/regression/null/best/common-only).

Strong caveat fidelity: seed noise +/-0.006, the null result, the regression, the head-only heavy-reverb gain, the Kirtland regression, and the still-unproven H2 efficiency claim are all shown; does not oversell.
Clear top-to-bottom sectioning (whole story -> trajectory -> ledger DAG -> per-species -> next steps) with an above-the-fold summary flow that lands the headline verdict at a glance.
weaknesses: Dataset framing is thin: no clip count (6,200), no split (70/15/15, ~930), and no imbalance magnitudes (480/<80/<45/52%) - the 'small data' claim is asserted qualitatively only.
The 'vs a bigger model' half of the hypothesis (H2) is never tested or quantified on the page; a reader cannot judge the efficiency claim, only that it is deferred.
Two xychart rendering blemishes (y-axis title overlapping ticks; redundant identical bar+line in the trajectory chart) slightly reduce legibility and encoding clarity.
At the glance level only 2 of 4 takeaways (partially-works + next-step) land; the regression (T2) and the stack/class-dependent-reverb finding (T3) require scrolling into the deep read.
evaluator_notes: The page is a genuinely honest, number-accurate research ledger for a technical collaborator - its strength is faithfulness and non-overselling. Accuracy is formula-driven at 12/15 conveyed = 8.0; the three absent facts are all dataset-characterization details (size, split, imbalance quantities) rather than results. Overall 7.3 reflects strong accuracy and structure held back by a weaker glance layer (only half the takeaways land above the fold) and minor chart-rendering craft issues.
